tier_rationale: Logitech's own technical-specifications page lists 'Corded USB, High Speed USB 2.0' as the sole connection with no wireless or Bluetooth capability, and the optional Logitech Webcam Software is listed as supported, not required. The camera enumerates as a standard UVC device, so it works with any application (Zoom, Teams, OBS, a browser) without installing anything.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes; the C270 only ever spoke to the computer it's plugged into over a USB cable, and it has no radio to phone home with even if it wanted to. Any application that can open a webcam can use it immediately — no Logitech account, no app, and no cloud service sits between the camera and the video call.

repairability.notes: Low-cost sealed plastic unit; not designed for disassembly or repair.

sources.supports: Manufacturer technical specifications: corded USB 2.0 connection, no wireless/Bluetooth listed, Logitech Webcam Software (LWS) listed as supported rather than required, resolution and system requirements.
Manufacturer product page: current price and general product description, compatibility with Zoom/Teams/Skype without a named vendor account requirement.

open_questions: The manufacturer pages do not use the term 'UVC' explicitly; UVC compliance is inferred from driverless cross-platform compatibility (works on macOS/ChromeOS with no Logitech software installed) rather than a direct manufacturer statement of the standard.
Logitech has no entry in data/vendors.json; no incident was found in this search, but a dedicated audit was not performed.
notes: One of the longest-running webcam SKUs on the market; still sold essentially unchanged, and a common baseline reference for a plain UVC webcam.
